## Setup

- `just setup` after a clone or `git worktree add`: it installs the hooks
  (`core.hooksPath .githooks`, including the Git LFS handoff), keeps `.worktrees`
  off the synced tree, and runs `scripts/gates/target-dir-check`.
- .cargo/config.toml and target/ are per-machine and must not reach another
  machine: both carry `user.com.dropbox.ignored=1`, so the shared tree holds neither.
  Without a .cargo/config.toml cargo builds into target/, which is what a fresh
  machine gets. To keep build output on a fast local disk, write your own
  .cargo/config.toml with `build.target-dir` and mark it ignored
  (`setfattr -n user.com.dropbox.ignored -v 1 .cargo`). A `target-dir` naming a path
  that exists on one machine only fails `cargo fmt` before any gate can run, so no
  commit is possible there.
- Every checkout builds into a target dir of its own: that `target-dir` is for the
  main checkout only. A worktree gets no `build.target-dir` or `build.build-dir` (or,
  under a parent config that sets one, both `target-dir = "target"` and
  `build-dir = "target"` in its own .cargo/config.toml) and builds into its own target/, which sits on local storage
  when .worktrees is a work-link symlink. Two checkouts sharing either dir serve each other's workspace
  crates as fresh (cargo keys them by root-relative path and checks them by mtime): a
  "no field" error the source contradicts, or a binary mixing the other tree's crates
  with no error at all. `just setup` after `git worktree add` and `just check` run
  `scripts/gates/target-dir-check`, which refuses a worktree that shares; the first build in a
  worktree is a full one.

## Gates

- Formatting uses nightly rustfmt (`rustup toolchain install nightly --profile minimal
  --component rustfmt`, then `rustup run nightly cargo fmt --all`), matching CI.
- Focused inner-loop `just test-one` always runs locally: for Rust,
  `just test-one -p niri <name-filter>` or `just test-one -E 'test(foo) | test(bar)'`;
  for Python, `just --set one_cmd 'env NIRI_TOOLING_FAST=0 python3 -m unittest' test-one tests.gates.test_gates`.
  When editing ImageMagick-backed capture scripts or tests, run
  `just --set one_cmd 'env NIRI_TOOLING_FAST=0 python3 -m unittest' test-one tests.capture.test_glass_optic_smoke tests.capture.test_glass_render_order_metrics tests.capture.test_glass_parameter_sweep`.
  Sequential discovery uses `env NIRI_TOOLING_FAST=0 python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t . 2>&1`
  (`NIRI_TOOLING_FAST=1` skips DriverCleanupTests and VtLibTests; only unset, `0`, `1`
  are valid). Fast tooling (`--fast`) runs one worker per module (largest first); full
  tooling (`--full`) runs lifecycle cases first, then remaining modules, capped by
  `min(worker_limit(), len(jobs))` (`10` default, up to `16` under `NEXTEST_TEST_THREADS`).
  Git-running test modules and the coordinator call `isolate(os.environ)` (`scripts/testing/hermetic_git.py`).
- Mandatory hygiene always runs locally: `just check-hygiene` (`tools/ops-check`,
  `tools/ops-docs` check, `scripts/gates/target-dir-check`, `scripts/testing/tooling_tests.py --check-paths`,
  `scripts/gates/identity-check`, `tasks check`, `scripts/gates/upstream-report --check`,
  `scripts/gates/package-pin --check`), commit-hook `scripts/gates/upstream-report --stage`, and
  `git lfs pre-push`. `just docs` regenerates identity regions from identity.toml.
  Pre-commit routes `tooling_full_paths` to `hook-pre-commit-full`, other code to
  `hook-pre-commit` (material docs/wiki included), and `docs_paths` to `hook-pre-commit-docs`.
- `.tt.toml` (`automatic_broad = false`) skips routine local runs of the 8 broad targets
  (`check-code`, `check-code-full`, `ci-test`, `ci-test-release`, `ci-tooling-test`,
  `test`, `test-fast`, `test-push-fast`), including inside `check`, `check-full`, `gate`,
  and `hook-*` (`hook-*` rows in `tools/tt` time mandatory staging/hygiene while broad
  child runs/skips record on `check-code*`, `test-push-fast`, and `test`).
- GitHub Actions `ci.yml` runs the full suite (including doctests, `ci-test`,
  `ci-test-release`, and Ubuntu `ci-tooling-test` with `OPTIONAL_SKIPS` in
  `scripts/testing/tooling_tests.py`) on every `origin` push under `TT_FORCE=1`. Deliberate local
  broad runs use `just test-full` or `TT_FORCE=1 just <recipe>` (for full Python tooling,
  `TT_FORCE=1 just --set fast_cmd 'env NIRI_TOOLING_FAST=0 python3 -m scripts.testing.tooling_tests --full' test-fast`).
- Rollback sets `automatic_broad = true` in `.tt.toml` (or removes `.tt.toml`), restores
  enabled cadence in `AGENTS.md` and `test_committed_root_policy_matches_broad_targets_and_forces_cleanly`,
  and records `policy: enabled at <RFC3339-UTC> revision <full-sha>` on material-ec0e0b.
- Recipes record runs through `tools/tt`. Host recipes use `host-budget run` to set
  `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS` and `NEXTEST_TEST_THREADS`; CI recipes do not need ops tooling.

## Layout

- Task records live in the project's records directory (`tasks where` names it).
  New design specs, implementation plans, briefs, handoffs and measurement
  evidence go there too, committed in the records repository, never in this tree.
- `docs/materials/`: the typed public references, indexed by its README;
  `docs/wiki/` and the README below its fork header are upstream niri's.
- `scripts/capture/`: the capture harnesses, described in
  `docs/materials/captures.md`.
- `scripts/gates/` and `scripts/testing/` hold repository maintenance; `tests/` mirrors
  tooling, with `tests/fixtures/` for test data. `tools/` holds only the ops copies
  named in `tools/README.md`, never edited here; this distribution home is interim.

- Layout deviation: upstream niri Rust crate/source layout is retained; reorganizing it would block upstream merges.
- Layout deviation: Python maintenance and C capture tooling stay in `scripts/` and `tests/` beside Rust, rather than separate language roots, because they support this application.
- Layout deviation: existing flat `scripts/capture/` lane prefixes and Python CLI filename spelling stay stable for documented operator entry points; new Python modules use snake_case.

## Rules

- Before changing anything under `src/render_helpers/` or the shaders, read
  `docs/materials/render-pipeline.md`: it is the pass order every rendering design
  assumes.
- Live captures that need an idle host (settle-gated traces, DRM power runs) are parked
  for `tasks quiet`. When the user starts a session from a TTY with the desktop stopped
  and hands the host over, run that queue yourself: one run at a time, the lane's pilot
  before any full run, and a `run:` note for every attempt. The harnesses are in
  `scripts/capture/`; `docs/materials/captures.md` gives the lanes, the gates and the
  known failure modes. Record each run's evidence in the records directory.
  A TTY has no display sleep. The reference host's monitor (G34WQC on DP-1)
  ignores DDC brightness writes, so do not try `display-dim set` there. Power
  the panel down once, at queue start, before the first preflight. Check that
  `pgrep -x niri` finds nothing, run
  `echo 4 | sudo -n tee /sys/class/graphics/fb0/blank`, and confirm that
  `/sys/class/drm/card1-DP-1/dpms` reads `Off` within a few seconds. Read the
  dpms file, not fb0's `blank` value, which goes stale. Never restore or
  re-blank it; leave it to the owner's keyboard or mouse. A missing sudo rule
  is a host setup fault, and a panel that stays `On` is reported; either way
  run with the display lit, because blanking never gates a run. With the
  desktop up, the capture hold powers the monitors off for each run and on
  again at release (start-only behaviour there is `ops-cab84f`). Say in the
  report that the display was powered down.
  The packages and host configuration every capture lane needs (sudoers, udev,
  AUR tools) are recorded in `docs/materials/capture-host-setup.md`.
- Before rebasing onto a new upstream release, read `docs/materials/upstream-divergence.md`:
  it carries the baseline, the acknowledged conflicts, and the rebase procedure. Never
  use `git merge-base` against upstream — this repository's history was rewritten and it
  returns a 2023 commit.
